crime.value: Anonymous bomb-scare hoax phone calls to Stevenson High School forcing evacuations; question: which absent student made the calls?
crime.quote: “This is no joke. A bomb is going to explode in your school in fifteen minutes.”

victim.value: No death; victims are the school/1800 students disrupted, and Lester Baines, the innocent truant framed by circumstance because he was absent on all call days
victim.quote: “And Lester Baines was absent.” ... “Just Lester Baines. He’s our boy.”

closed_world.value: Stevenson High School's student body, narrowed by attendance records: only boys absent during class hours on all call dates
closed_world.quote: “all of the calls came during times when classes were in session. And that means that only a student who was absent could have made them.”

culprit_and_motive.value: Dave, the narrator-detective's own son, made the first two calls as a prank to disrupt school; the third call was made by Jim himself to clear Dave by giving him an alibi
culprit_and_motive.quote: “Lester didn’t make those bomb calls. I did.” ... “I did it as a joke. I just wanted to pep things up.”

resolution.value: Elimination by attendance records leaves two suspects; Jim confronts Dave with the logic, Dave confesses rather than let Lester suffer, and Jim admits his own cover-up call and phones Lester's father
resolution.quote: “I guess I ought to tell them I made all of the calls, Dad” ... “Thanks, son. I’ll tell them what I did.”

investigator.value: Jim, a police detective narrating in first person, who is also the concealed perpetrator of the third call and father of the culprit
investigator.quote: Yes, Lester Baines could have made those first two phone calls. And I had made the third.

suspect_architecture.value: Narrowed by attendance records from 96 absent students to three boys absent on both call days: Lester Baines (no alibi, playing hookey, failing grades), a boy hospitalized out of state (eliminated), and Dave — the narrator's own son, the actual culprit, shielded by his father's position.
suspect_architecture.quote: "And that left us with just two suspects. Lester Baines—and you."

red_herring.value: The narrator himself makes a third bomb-scare call at 1:20 while Dave is in class, manufacturing an alibi for his son and directing all suspicion onto Lester Baines; Lester's evasive lies about a cold and swimming reinforce the false trail.
red_herring.quote: "Yes, Lester Baines could have made those first two phone calls. And I had made the third."

clue_fairness.value: Fair-play cues are planted early: the story opens with the narrator himself placing the call through a handkerchief from a gas station across from the police station, before any detection begins; Dave's presence at the school and eagerness about the cancelled history exam are also shown to the reader.
clue_fairness.quote: "I spoke through the handkerchief over the mouthpiece. 'This is no joke. A bomb is going to explode in your school in fifteen minutes.'"

social_world.value: Suburban school-and-police hierarchy: principal, teachers, detectives, and working-class families; a father's police authority lets him quietly exempt his own son from questioning while another family is pressured into lying for theirs.
social_world.quote: "Not myself. But the department got around to seeing all of them."

alibi.value: Baines' parents falsely swear Lester was home all day; Lester's real alibi is truant swimming and unwitnessed. Dave's alibi — being in class during the third call — is genuine but fabricated for him by his father's own hoax call.
alibi.quote: "Right here," Baines said again. "My wife and I will swear to it."

reveal_mechanic.value: Psychological confrontation in the garage: the father lays out the elimination logic and waits; Dave, unnerved, confesses to the first two calls, then the father discloses that he made the third himself.
reveal_mechanic.quote: "Lester didn't make those bomb calls. I did."

media_and_audience.value: Bomb scares are reported in the newspaper and treated by students as a welcome break from exams rather than a crime; police assume public opinion that a disgruntled student is responsible.
media_and_audience.quote: "I read in the paper that there was another bomb scare at Stevenson this morning."

investigator_wound.value: Detective Jim's paternal blind spot and loyalty: he cannot believe his own son capable of it, skips questioning him, then commits a crime to protect him — pitting his duty against his fatherhood.
investigator_wound.quote: "Other men's boys might have done such a thing, but not my boy."

victims_enemies.value: No murder victim; the 'victim' is Stevenson High School itself, targeted by a bored student. The only grievance texture is generic adolescent resentment — bad marks, hated teachers, or a desire to 'pep things up' before a history exam.
victims_enemies.quote: "A boy decides he hates one of the teachers or the whole school because he's getting bad marks."

suspect_wounds.value: Lester Baines is a chronic truant with failing grades who skipped school to avoid two tests and lied to his parents about a cold — so every honest answer he gives sounds like a cover story, and his parents' instinct to lie for him deepens the appearance of guilt.
suspect_wounds.quote: "I didn't have a cold today. I just stayed away from school. Mom and Dad don't know that."

unreliable_frame.value: The first-person narrator, Detective Jim, is the story's liar: he opens by placing the third bomb call himself and then narrates the investigation of it without disclosing this until the end. His account is suppression rather than falsehood.
unreliable_frame.quote: "Yes, Lester Baines could have made those first two phone calls. And I had made the third."

setting_as_constraint.value: The school's attendance records function as a closed timetable: calls came only while classes were in session, so the caller must be a student marked absent at that hour. Jim exploits this by phoning at 1:20 from a gas station across from the station, knowing Dave was present that afternoon and would be eliminated.
setting_as_constraint.quote: "all of the calls came during times when classes were in session. And that means that only a student who was absent could have made them."

evidence_type.value: Documentary — school attendance records cross-referenced across three call dates, narrowing 96 absentees to three, then to one; supplemented by testimonial confession.
evidence_type.quote: "only three boys had been absent on both this morning and on the day of the first phone call."

false_suspect.value: Lester Baines, innocent of the calls but absent on all three dates because he was truant swimming; deliberately left as the sole suspect by Jim's fabricated third call.

technical_detail.value: Police procedure of cross-indexing absentee lists against call times, plus the fact that the calls were all local — which eliminates the boy hospitalized five hundred miles away with scarlet fever; the handkerchief over the mouthpiece keeps the voice 'muffled and indistinct.'
technical_detail.quote: "He's in a hospital five hundred miles away from here—and the phone calls were all local."

moral_ambiguity.value: The detective-culprit commits a crime out of paternal love, not malice — timing the call so no one could be hurt, and hoping Lester would prove guilty anyway; his son's confession redeems both, and Jim chooses to turn himself in.
moral_ambiguity.quote: "a father doesn't always think too clearly when it involves his son. And I was hoping that it might turn out to be Lester after all."
